operator.name: Steam Ship Sudan (Voyageurs du Monde)
operator.display_rule: Information only. No photos until permission is given. Attribute the operator's own claims (launch year, the Agatha Christie connection, engineering).

propulsion_support.text: Its triple-expansion steam engine still turns the paddle wheels, now fired by diesel rather than coal, with an auxiliary thruster to help.

deck_plan.note: Only a 2007 plan exists, with different cabin names and 21 units. Historical reference, not shown.

on_board.food: The operator describes a menu created with chef Jean Imbert around Egyptian ingredients such as Nile fish, lentils, spices, citrus and hibiscus.

wifi.value: Reported aboard, patchy on a January 2023 voyage

cabin_amenities.value: Air conditioning, internal telephone, safe, hairdryer, 220 V sockets (2024 report)

suitability.children: Children under six are not accepted.
suitability.less_suited_to: Families travelling with children under six.

fleet_defaults.route_note: From late November to mid-February, low water stops the ship sailing between Luxor and Qena, and an alternative programme applies. Abydos is visited by road.

cabin.name: Cabin
cabin.feature: Named and decorated individually, with two windows onto the shared promenade deck.

suite.name: Suite
suite.feature: Named and decorated individually, with larger panoramic windows. The Odilo suite has a private deck.

vessels.name: Steam Ship Sudan
vessels.summary: A historic side-wheel paddle steamer, launched in 1921 according to its operator, with 18 cabins and six suites across three decks.
vessels.description: Every cabin and suite has its own name and decoration, from Agatha Christie to Naguib Mahfouz. Agatha Christie cruised the Nile in 1933, four years before Death on the Nile, and the ship’s operator identifies the Sudan as the steamer that inspired the novel.

programme.title: Aswan and Philae
programme.text: Board in Aswan and visit Philae Temple. The first night is spent in Aswan.

programme.title: Abydos

programme.text: Visit the tombs and temples of the west bank, then leave the ship in Luxor. Entry to Nefertari’s tomb depends on availability.
